paragraphs.content: I dislike the idea that i can forget scripts altogether. This kind of happened with Hindi, but a 10-page assignment later i could sufficiently write up an impromptu apology letter that was convincing enough to not warrant scrutiny by my Hindi professor. This same principle, when applied toa language like malayalam inspires this odd feeling, recognition-driven nostalgia. What I mean to say is that this script, much like hindi up until recently held more of a generic semiotic meaning to me. It is like the image of a place or the image of a time in my life, rather than a blunt meaning at the base of inspiration for more nuanced thought, the image of letters strung together as a whole inspired the singular emotion of the aforementioned nostalgia and perhaps dread too. Dread in not knowing and dread in maybe never knowing.

I was at this book store here in pune that i love where i was flipping through books in the language section and thinking about speaking in them and stuff, as one does i suppose, specifically german which i spoke with an okayish proficiency once upon a time and that got me rather very excited and i realised how much i just love being able to speak in different languages. I think I kind of just love the structure it can give to thought, like the way you think and what precedes and follows stuff, that kinda thing. New ways to think are, therefore to me a new way to exist, its like a whole new life i get to unlock and i kind of love that idea. I get to be more of myself, see and re live parts of my life that are very mundane again and again, i like the idea of practicing this in a sense, and practicing being live, sucking at it and getting better. I like that.

I think the most poignant example for all this is my love for math, and physics too, but well, math is the underlying syntax. It gives you so much structure. This initially feels restrictive, but i think the more you live with it, and in it, the more you can speak in it. I know that's a fairly obvious observation about any language per se, but i think what makes math different from it is how whether you are right or wrong in your practice of it is so binary. There can't be any grey, and that is extremely harsh to people who thrive in the grey. I think you can find these areas in math where things are grey, where you can mess around, and I believe that's how you make any progress at all. There is a big obstacle that stands in the way of this, that being that math almost requires that you look at things as abstractions, the very best math infact (in my humble opinion); category theory abstracts things even further. I like this though there is this clarity in thinking that gives me what I can't seem to get elsewhere. However much a tool as that is it is far more pertinent to me that i express myself and be able to do that in any which way is the only thing actually genuinely makes me enjoy this even though its a lot and its painful and it just can tire you out.
